impression: Two axial levels of an unenhanced chest CT, upper thorax and carina, both technically unremarkable on soft-tissue window. Lungs are well aerated bilaterally and extend to the chest wall on both frames, with normal-calibre branching pulmonary vessels that become appropriately prominent at the hila on the carinal frame. No consolidation, mass, pleural fluid, or pneumothorax at either level. Airway is midline and non-deviated from trachea through to the bifurcation, with no visible intraluminal lesion or extrinsic compression. Mediastinal soft tissue is homogeneous with no discrete mass or clearly enlarged node, though on an unenhanced study nodes and unopacified vessels are isodense and cannot be separated; the subcarinal space in particular cannot be assessed. A rounded left paravertebral contour on the carinal frame is consistent with the descending thoracic aorta in normal position. Sternum, ribs, scapulae, and thoracic vertebrae appear intact with no fracture or lytic or sclerotic lesion. Chest wall soft tissues are mildly bulkier on the left than the right across both frames, most likely positional or habitus-related. No discrete abnormality recorded at either level.
limitations: Two axial levels only. The rest of the volume is unassessed — most of both lungs, the upper abdomen, and the lower thorax were never seen.
Soft-tissue window on both frames. Pulmonary nodules, ground-glass, emphysema, and interstitial disease are effectively not assessable without a lung window; neither frame excludes them.
Non-contrast. Mediastinal and hilar nodes cannot be distinguished from unopacified vessels, and no vascular assessment (embolism, dissection, aneurysm) is possible.
No DICOM metadata. Contrast phase, window, and slice levels are inferred from appearance; slice thickness and study date are unknown.
No burned-in callipers, scale bar, or HU ROI, so no size or attenuation value is recorded — any measurement here would be an estimate, not data.
The two frames are assumed to belong to one acquisition on visual grounds, not on metadata. If they are in fact separate studies, this record merges two studies and must be split.
A negative read at two levels is not a normal study.
